passages.locator: freedom of mind, reason, cultural exchange
passages.excerpt_preview: His arguments joined freedom of mind, reason, cultural exchange and criticism of narrow identity.
Tagore praised Gandhi’s political achievement while disagreeing with him on nationalism, education, science and some forms of protest.

passages.locator: spiritual image that did not represent the range
passages.excerpt_preview: Sen cautions that Tagore’s international reputation later narrowed around a spiritual image that did not represent the range of his work.

passages.locator: reprinted repeatedly before the Nobel announcement
passages.excerpt_preview: The English Gitanjali appeared in London in 1913 and was reprinted repeatedly before the Nobel announcement.
martya Sen describes Tagore as a towering figure in Bengali literature whose poetry, novels, short stories, essays and songs remain widely present in India and Bangladesh.
